# A Theory of Conditional Collapse under Low-Rank Weight-Space Ablations: I. The Single-Block Theory and Synthetic Validation

- **Authors**: Abdallah Khemais
- **Venue**: cs.LG
- **Published**: 2026-08-04
- **Source**: arxiv
- **Link**: <https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03620>
- **PDF**: <https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.03620v1>
- **Topics**: reasoning-interpretability
- **Relevance score**: reasoning-interpretability 0.50

## In one line

Proves that activation patching and weight-space ablation measure two different quantities — a carrier's donor-receiver contrast versus its absolute level at the receiver — which neither bounds, gives an exact if-and-only-if criterion for when ablating a subset collapses a conditional onto one branch, and then withdraws its own clean empirical separation when it fails out of sample.

## Problem

Mechanistic interpretability certifies that a component is causally responsible for a behaviour by intervening on it, and two families of intervention dominate. Patching replaces a component's activation inside one forward pass; ablation edits the parameters that generate every forward pass. Both are read as evidence for the same informal claim, and nothing in current practice specifies when they should agree. Existing evidence that they need not — the compensation of downstream layers after an ablation, and redundant or superposed codes — is a collection of cautions rather than a statement of what each one measures.

## Contributions

- An if-and-only-if criterion for a weight-space ablation to collapse a conditional onto a single unconditional branch: the removal must be symmetric on the matched pair and no contrast may survive outside the ablated set, with the polarity of the resulting error fixed by the pair's mean margin
- A robust form of that criterion — the same computation gives an exact error identity rather than an estimate, so a condition stated as two exact equalities degrades gracefully into a tolerance condition instead of describing a null set
- An exact naming of what the two interventions move: patching a carrier shifts the readout by its donor-receiver contrast, ablating it shifts the readout by its absolute level at the receiver, and neither bounds the other
- A construction of matched pairs on which every single-carrier patch flips the decision while no single-carrier ablation does — the redundancy regime where patching overstates importance and ablation understates it, produced with no repair mechanism at all
- An exact first-order formula with a provably second-order remainder for the one composition where the additive picture is architecturally false, an attention head and its own layer's MLP separated by a normalization, which vanishes identically when the MLP alone is ablated but not in general when a head is

## Method

The idealized setting writes a residual block's output as an unconditional part plus a sum of carriers, each a fixed direction times a scalar selector, read out by a linear functional whose sign is the decision. A matched pair is two inputs that should receive the same answer through opposite branches of the conditional. Deleting a subset of carriers is shown to be exactly what a low-rank edit of one component's own weights does to the residual stream — an identity rather than an approximation — and the analysis proceeds in that output space. Everything rests on residual additivity, low-rank support, a stable base computation and a linear readout, with the load-bearing assumptions stated as such rather than buried. The empirical section trains five small transformers on a synthetic conditional task where a marker selects between two surface formats demanding the same answer, so each branch has one systematic wrong answer and a collapse is observable rather than merely a drop in accuracy. Carriers are found by greedy patching search, ablated in weight space by projecting their donor-receiver activation deltas out of the corresponding weight matrices, over three nested subsets per instance. A second freshly trained instance with a different conditional mechanism and a smaller architecture repeats the checks that do not presuppose the matched-pair structure.

## Results

The predictions are realized rather than vacuous. Redundancy and low rank hold on all five instances, and ablation collapses the network onto an unconditional reader on four of them. The fifth is the informative one: two *nested* subsets collapse the same trained weights onto *opposite* readers, each with the untouched format retained at 0.96 or better — a rank-one head alone gives the inverted reader at 0.93, and that head together with its own block's MLP gives the literal reader at 0.977. The idealized model forbids this, so at least one subset must violate a collapse hypothesis, and the paper traces which. The dissociation is confirmed on a single site where patching gives a median recovery of 1.043 with an 0.85 flip rate — recovery above one being the overshoot signature — while ablating the weights feeding that same site leaves the receiver format correct on 57% of inputs: patch-sufficient, far from ablation-necessary, on the same component of the same network. The collapse certificate turns out rarely available for a structural reason worth recording: the mean margin it must exceed is small by construction (median 0.083 of the pair contrast) while the tolerances are of the order of the margins themselves (0.14 and 0.21), so the sufficient condition misses by a median factor of 5.3 and fires on 10.0% of pair-configurations — though it discriminates rather than being uniformly pessimistic, with realized collapse rate rising from 32% to 57% to 88% across certificate-rate bands. The paper's own headline empirical claim does not survive its out-of-sample test, and it says so. A clean numerical band separating configurations that the idealized model describes from those it does not, read off the original 14, was frozen along with its decision rule and applied to all 39 subsets including 25 never used to fix anything, on a third disjoint probe seed: nine violate it, six out of sample, seven land inside the supposedly empty band, and three of the original 14 change sides on mere re-measurement. What survives is a monotone association at Spearman -0.83 over all 39, -0.85 on the held-out 25 alone, with the pass rate falling 7/8 to 6/8 to 1/7 across terciles of interaction magnitude. The second task and architecture reproduce all of it, including a polarity reversal and the same monotone relationship at -0.90.

## Limitations

The paper's discussion is the most careful in this archive and states the bounds itself. The three central results rest on the additive decomposition and the linear readout and use no property of transformers at all; what they do *not* establish is that a real network satisfies that decomposition, which is why the interaction theorem exists and why its scope is delimited from inside the model rather than assumed. On the experiments: 'what the experiments establish is weaker than what a first pass suggested, and we prefer to say so in both places' — the theory identifies the right quantity, not a usable decision threshold, and supplying one would require showing the cutoff transfers across networks, which five instances do not. What remains open is stated precisely: the criterion says when a given subset collapses but gives no procedure for constructing one, so it does not license designing an ablation to steer polarity; the interaction analysis does not extend past the block containing the two carriers, and multi-layer carrier interactions are uncovered; and everything empirical is a small transformer on a synthetic task, with the extension to a real pretrained model deferred to a companion analysis whose own result is described in advance as genuinely mixed.

## Why it matters here

- **reasoning-interpretability**: This turns the archive's standing caution about interpretability instruments into an identity. The archive already holds that a direction's discriminability licenses no claim about what steering it does; this paper establishes the parallel statement one level up — patching and ablation are different operators on different objects, they measure a carrier's contrast and its absolute level respectively, and neither bounds the other, with an explicit construction where every single-carrier patch is sufficient and no single-carrier ablation is necessary. Any claim in this archive resting on one of those two interventions should now name which quantity it measured. The empirical conduct is worth as much as the theorem. A clean separation found on 14 configurations was frozen as a rule and tested on 25 held-out ones, failed, and was withdrawn in favour of the weaker monotone claim the data support — including the detail that three of the original 14 flip sides on re-measurement alone. That is the discipline the archive's own findings on baseline validity and randomized controls keep pointing toward, executed by the authors against themselves. The polarity reversal is the concrete warning to carry: two *nested* ablated subsets collapsed the same trained network onto opposite unconditional readers, so enlarging a subset that already produces a clean collapse can reverse rather than deepen it.

## Abstract

Activation patching and weight-space ablation both claim a component is causally responsible for a behavior, yet they act on different objects: one forward pass versus the parameters behind every forward pass. We ask when they agree. We study an idealized model where a conditional computation is carried additively through a residual stream, $F(x)=F_0(x)+\sum_iα_i(x)v_i$, read out by a linear functional, and prove three exact results. First, deleting a subset of carriers collapses a matched input pair onto the same unconditional output \emph{if and only if} the removal is symmetric on the pair and leaves no outside contrast; the error is deterministic, and we give its exact form even when the two conditions hold only approximately. Second, patching a carrier moves the readout by its donor-receiver \emph{contrast}, while ablating it moves the readout by its \emph{absolute level}; neither bounds the other, and we construct pairs where every single-carrier patch flips the decision while no single-carrier ablation does. Third, for an attention head composed with its own layer's normalization and MLP, we derive an exact first-order interaction formula with a provably second-order remainder, vanishing identically when only the MLP is ablated but not, in general, when a head is. Small transformers trained on a synthetic conditional task illustrate all three predictions: across thirty-nine ablation configurations the measured interaction is strongly rank-correlated with the idealized model's predictive accuracy (Spearman $-0.83$), and a second task and architecture reproduces the same pattern, including a further polarity reversal. The single-block interaction result extends past one residual block, and the synthetic validation is tested against a real pretrained model, in a companion paper that takes this theory further along both axes.
